NVIDIA Control Panel

Step-by-step guide with screenshots – every click is marked in red.

LAG|ZERØ / OPTIMIZED NVIDIA SETTINGS

Goal of this guide

Set the listed NVIDIA 3D settings to the given values one after another. Work through the steps from top to bottom and don't skip any setting.
Basic rule: if a setting is already correct, leave it unchanged and go straight to the next step. If it is wrong, change it to the given value.

Part 1 – Open the NVIDIA Control Panel

1
Open the NVIDIA Control Panel
Open the NVIDIA Control Panel in Windows.
Check: the NVIDIA Control Panel must be open.
How to find it: right-click an empty spot on the desktop → “NVIDIA Control Panel”. On Windows 11 it is often under “Show more options” first. Alternatively press the Windows key and type “NVIDIA Control Panel”.
!Pre-check (one time only)
On the left click “Adjust image settings with preview” and select “Use the advanced 3D image settings”. Otherwise the driver will not use your settings from the next steps. Then continue with step 2.
2
Go to the 3D settings
On the left click “Manage 3D settings”.
Check: the 3D settings page must be shown.
3
Select Global Settings
At the top click the “Global Settings” tab.
Check: the global NVIDIA settings must be visible.
4
Work from top to bottom
Go through the settings in the following order. For each setting, check the current value first.
If the value is correct: change nothing and move on.
If the value is wrong: open the setting, select the correct value and move on.

Part 2 – Set the settings one by one

5
Antialiasing – FXAA
Find “Antialiasing – FXAA”. Check the current value.
Target: Off
If it is not set to “Off”, open the drop-down and select “Off”.
Why: Smooths edges after rendering. “Off” saves a little GPU work.
6
Antialiasing – Mode
Find “Antialiasing – Mode” (German UI: “Antialiasing – Modus”).
Target: Application-controlled
If needed, open the drop-down and select “Application-controlled”.
Why: The game keeps control over anti-aliasing.
7
Antialiasing – Setting
Find “Antialiasing – Setting” (German UI: “Antialiasing – Einstellung”).
Target: Application-controlled
If needed, set it to “Application-controlled”.
Why: The game decides how strong the anti-aliasing is.
8
Antialiasing – Gamma correction
Find “Antialiasing – Gamma correction” (German UI: “Antialiasing – Gammakorrektur”).
Target: On
If needed, set it to “On”.
Why: Improves how smoothed edges look by using gamma-corrected calculation.
9
Antialiasing – Transparency
Find “Antialiasing – Transparency” (German UI: “Antialiasing – Transparenz”).
Target: Off
If needed, set it to “Off”.
Why: Smooths transparent textures like fences, grates or foliage. “Off” saves extra GPU work.
10
Anisotropic filtering
Find “Anisotropic filtering” (German UI: “Anisotrope Filterung”).
Target: Application-controlled
If needed, select “Application-controlled”.
Why: Improves the sharpness of textures seen at an angle, e.g. floors and roads.
11
Ambient occlusion
Find “Ambient occlusion” (German UI: “Umgebungsverdeckung”).
Target: Off
If needed, set it to “Off”.
Why: Adds soft shadows in contact and ambient areas. “Off” saves GPU performance.
12
Power management mode
Find “Power management mode” (German UI: “Energieverwaltungsmodus”).
Target: Prefer maximum performance
Open the drop-down and select “Prefer maximum performance”.
Why: The GPU keeps higher clocks when needed. This can increase power draw and heat.
13
Preferred refresh rate
Find “Preferred refresh rate” (German UI: “Bevorzugte Aktualisierungsrate”).
Target: Highest available
If needed, select “Highest available”.
Why: Sets which available refresh rate is preferred.
14
Low Latency Mode
Find “Low Latency Mode” (German UI: “Modus für geringe Latenz”).
Target: On
If needed, set it to “On”.
Why: Limits the number of frames the driver queues before rendering.
15
Shader Cache Size
Find “Shader Cache Size” (German UI: “Shadercache”).
Target: 100 GB
If needed, set the value to “100 GB”.
Why: Sets the storage limit for compiled shader cache data. The value is not a direct FPS control.
16
Texture filtering – Anisotropic sample optimization
Find “Texture filtering – Anisotropic sample optimization” (German UI: “Texturfilterung – Anisotrope Filteroptimierung”).
Target: On
If needed, set it to “On”.
Why: Can improve performance with a possible small loss in filtering quality.
17
Texture filtering – Negative LOD bias
Find “Texture filtering – Negative LOD bias” (German UI: “Texturfilterung – Negativer LOD-Bias”).
Target: Allow
If needed, select “Allow”.
Why: Can make textures look sharper but may also cause shimmering.
18
Texture filtering – Quality
Find “Texture filtering – Quality” (German UI: “Texturfilterung – Qualität”).
Target: High performance
If needed, select “High performance”.
Why: Prioritises high frame rate over maximum filtering quality.
19
Texture filtering – Trilinear optimization
Find “Texture filtering – Trilinear optimization” (German UI: “Texturfilterung – Trilineare Optimierung”).
Target: On
If needed, set it to “On”.
Why: Can speed up texture filtering with a small possible quality difference.
20
Threaded optimization
Find “Threaded optimization”.
Target: Auto
If needed, select “Auto”.
Why: Lets the driver decide whether several CPU cores are used for certain driver tasks.
21
Vertical sync
Find “Vertical sync” (German UI: “Vertikale Synchronisierung”).
Target: Off
If needed, set it to “Off”.
Why: “Off” minimises extra sync waiting time and allows maximum FPS but can cause tearing.
22
Virtual Reality – Variable rate supersampling
Find “Virtual Reality – Variable rate supersampling” (German UI: “Virtual Reality – Supersampling”).
Target: Off
If needed, set it to “Off”.
Why: “Off” saves GPU performance. “On” can improve sharpness but costs more rendering power.
23
Virtual Reality pre-rendered frames
Find “Virtual Reality pre-rendered frames” (German UI: “Vorgerenderte Virtual-Reality-Einzelbilder”).
Target: 1
If needed, set the value to “1”.
Why: A low value can reduce latency. “1” keeps the render queue short.
24
Vulkan/OpenGL present method
Find “Vulkan/OpenGL present method” (German UI: “Vulkan/OpenGL – Present-Methode”).
Target: Auto
If needed, select “Auto”.
Why: Lets the driver and application choose the right presentation path.
25
OpenGL rendering GPU
Find “OpenGL rendering GPU” (German UI: “OpenGL rendernde GPU”).
Target: Auto
If needed, select “Auto”.
Why: Sets which GPU is used for OpenGL applications. “Auto” picks the right GPU.
26
OpenGL GDI compatibility
Find “OpenGL GDI compatibility” (German UI: “OpenGL GDI-Kompatibilität”).
Target: Auto
If needed, select “Auto”.
Why: Controls compatibility between OpenGL and older Windows GDI functions.

Part 3 – Apply the settings

27
Check the whole list
Go through the settings once more from top to bottom.
Check that every value matches its target.
28
Apply the changes
At the bottom right click “Apply” (German UI: “Übernehmen”).
Wait until the NVIDIA Control Panel has applied the change.

Done

You are done when all listed settings have been checked, changed where needed and then saved with “Apply”.

Appendix – what the settings mean

The detailed explanations are an appendix. The step-by-step guide shows what to click; the INFO buttons explain what each setting does.
Click the i next to a setting to open its explanation.

1
Antialiasing – FXAA
Off

What does it do?

Post-processing anti-aliasing. Smooths edges after rendering but can make the image look slightly soft.

Effect

Off saves a little GPU work and leaves the actual anti-aliasing to the game.

What does it do?

Decides whether the NVIDIA driver forces anti-aliasing or the game decides itself.

Effect

The game keeps control and avoids conflicts with its own AA implementation.
